```{r}
#| label: setup
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(knitr)
tab_dir <- file.path("..", "results", "tables")
fig_dir <- file.path("..", "results", "figures")
k <- function(f, digits = 3) kable(
  read_csv(file.path(tab_dir, f), show_col_types = FALSE), digits = digits)
# Slim display for contrast tables: combine the HL estimate with its CI so
# wide tables fit a portrait page without wrapping.
fmt_contrast <- function(f) {
  d <- read_csv(file.path(tab_dir, f), show_col_types = FALSE)
  d$hl <- sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", d$hl_est, d$hl_l, d$hl_u)
  keep <- c("contrast", "n_pairs", "W", "p", "p_holm", "hl", "r_rb")
  keep <- keep[keep %in% names(d)]
  out <- d[, keep]
  names(out) <- c("Contrast", "n", "W", "p", "p (Holm)", "HL [95% CI]", "r")[seq_along(keep)]
  kable(out, digits = 4)
}
```

## Abstract

Methanolic extracts of *Azadirachta indica* and *Moringa oleifera* (leaves,
stem bark, roots, seeds) were tested against *Trypanosoma congolense* and
*T. evansi* in motility assays and in albino mice (N = 16 plant × part ×
parasite blocks; group means of n = 3 mice). Both parasites show a clear,
monotonic dose response: *T. evansi* significantly (Friedman p = 0.006; top
three doses beat control, Holm 0.039) and *T. congolense* suggestively
(Friedman p = 0.074; 100 mg/ml Holm 0.071). At 100 mg/ml the mean peak
parasitaemia is zero in both parasites with no deaths, against universal
mortality in Negative Controls. No evidence separates the two plants
(paired p = 1.0, HL 0.3 [−14.7, 20.5]). All inference is block-level and
rank-based; every headline claim survived leave-one-block-out sensitivity
analysis.

## 1. Aim, objectives and section map

The aim of this study is to comparatively evaluate the anti-trypanosomal
activity of methanolic extracts of the leaves, stem bark, roots and seeds of
*Azadirachta indica* and *Moringa oleifera* against *Trypanosoma congolense*
and *T. evansi* (thesis §1.8.1). Each specific objective (§1.8.2) is addressed
in a dedicated results section — extraction (i) in §5.1, phytochemical
characterisation (ii) in §5.2, the motility assay (iii) in §5.3, in-vivo
infectivity (iv) in §5.4, superiority (v) in §5.5 — each opening with
exploratory description before any inference. Diagnostics, limitations and
references follow in §6–§8.

## 2. Data and experimental design

Source data are group means of n = 3 mice per group, parsed from Sheet 2 of
the study workbook into tidy CSVs (`analysis/data/`, builder
`analysis/R/01_build_datasets.R`). Within any block each of the 7 groups is
therefore n = 1 (descriptive only); the analytical unit is the **block
(N = 16; 8 per plant, 8 per parasite)**. Plant contrasts pair by part ×
parasite (8 pairs); parasite contrasts pair by plant × part (8 pairs).
Controls appear as labelled in the source (identities/doses unstated), so the
Positive Control is an assay-validity reference only.

## 3. Endpoints

Parasitaemia (LEV 0–5 ordinal): primary **AUC** (death-censored trapezoid,
always with mortality), supported by peak LEV, clearance day and day-40
status — day-40 alone is degenerate (0/112 positive; positivity peaks ~30%
at days 9–14). Motility: TTI, t120, mean proportion motile (key: `+ Active`,
`− No motility`; `+-` → NA, 2 cells). Weight/PCV: Δ = Post − Pre with
literature flags (anaemia: Post < 35% or ≥ 25% drop, severe < 30%/≥ 40%;
weight signal ≥ 10% loss, severe ≥ 20%). Raw LEV > 5 (42 cells) capped to 5
with `lev_raw` preserved and flagged. Missing in-vivo values = death
(adopted convention, never imputed).

## 4. Statistical methods

Description first (trajectories, endpoint tables, flags), then rank-based
inference: Friedman blocked by block for dose trends with pooled Spearman ρ
on log10 dose; paired Wilcoxon signed-rank (exact when tie-free, otherwise
the continuity-corrected normal approximation — §6) for dose-vs-control
post-hocs and plant/parasite contrasts, with matched-pairs rank-biserial
effect size (|r| ≥ 0.11/0.28/0.43) and Hodges–Lehmann median difference with
95% CI. Dose-vs-control families are Holm-adjusted per parasite; plant and
parasite questions are independent and uncorrected across questions.
Per-block trend tests at n = 1 lack power, so only the blocked Friedman is
inferential. Significance p < 0.05, p-values supplementary to effects.
Script: `analysis/R/02_analysis.R` (statistics only, no ML).

## 5.1. Objective i — methanolic extraction

Objective i is a laboratory procedure with no statistical component — no
yields or replicates are recorded — so there is nothing to estimate or test.
It is noted here solely to keep the objective map complete.

## 5.2. Objective ii — phytochemical contents

Exploration first: screening recovered all 12 compound classes, with
richness concentrated in leaves and seeds (@fig-rich; @tbl-phyto). *M.
oleifera* leaves carry the broadest profile (9 of 12) and stem bark the
sparsest in both plants; the presence matrix (@fig-phyto-hm) shows no single
plant-specific signature compound. With only eight plant × part combinations
no test has power, so inference stops here: compound–efficacy overlays are
tabulated exploratorily without tests
(`phytochemical_efficacy_overlay.csv`).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-phyto
#| tbl-cap: Phytochemical richness per plant and part (descriptive).
k("phytochemical_richness.csv", 0)
```

## 5.3. Objective iii — in-vitro motility dose response

Exploration shows a textbook gradient (@fig-tti): median TTI rises from 15
min at 100 mg/ml (both parasites, zero censoring) through ~45–105 min at
intermediate doses to fully censored Negative Controls, while mean t120
motility climbs from 0 to 0.67–1.0 (@tbl-tti). Trajectories (@fig-mot-traj)
confirm rapid kill at high doses and the expected Positive Control profile
(+ at t = 0, immobile thereafter). Inference follows the description: the
blocked dose trend is highly significant for both parasites (@tbl-mot-dose:
*congolense* Q = 27.75, p < 0.001, ρ = −0.70; *evansi* Q = 30.32, p < 0.001,
ρ = −0.88). Post-hoc dose-vs-control contrasts (@tbl-mot-posthoc) carry
large consistent effects (rank-biserial −1; HL ≈ −0.83 *congolense*,
−0.89 *evansi* at 100 mg/ml) that sit just above Holm-adjusted significance
(0.065, 0.052) — strong but formally inconclusive at N = 8; lower doses match
the control.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-tti
#| tbl-cap: Exploratory TTI and t120 summaries per dose (medians; censored groups never immobilise).
k("explore_tti.csv")
```

![Time to immobilisation by dose (black = median; x = censored)](`r file.path(fig_dir, "explore_tti_dose.png")`){#fig-tti}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-mot-dose
#| tbl-cap: Motility dose-response on mean proportion motile (Friedman blocked by block; Spearman on log10 dose).
k("dose_response_motility.csv")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-mot-posthoc
#| tbl-cap: Post-hoc motility contrasts vs Negative Control (paired Wilcoxon; Holm per parasite).
```

## 5.4. Objective iv — in-vivo infectivity

### Parasitaemia

Exploration first: peak parasitaemia falls monotonically with dose —
100 mg/ml holds mean peak at zero in both parasites with no deaths, against
peak 5 and universal mortality in Negative Controls (@tbl-peak;
@fig-peak). Clearance days shorten and day-40 zeros accumulate with dose,
while mortality concentrates in low-dose and control groups (@fig-mort).
Trajectories (@fig-para-traj) rise from day 1, peak near days 9–14 and
resolve in survivors. Inference: cumulative burden (AUC) falls monotonically
with log-concentration (@fig-auc) — significantly for *T. evansi*
(@tbl-dose: Q = 14.51, p = 0.006, ρ = −0.51) and suggestively for
*T. congolense* (Q = 8.52, p = 0.074, ρ = −0.42). Post-hocs (@tbl-para-posthoc)
confirm *evansi* 100/10/0.5 mg/ml in all eight blocks (W = 0, exact
p = 0.008, Holm 0.039; HL ≈ −50/−50/−44 AUC-days); *congolense* 100 mg/ml is
suggestive only (Holm 0.071). No parasite-level AUC difference (p = 0.46).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-peak
#| tbl-cap: Exploratory peak, clearance and mortality per dose (means/medians over 8 blocks).
k("explore_peak_mortality.csv")
```

### Body weight and PCV

Exploration: mean weight and PCV paths across the three timepoints run
roughly flat for both plants and parasites (@fig-wp-traj), and deltas centre
near zero with wide scatter (@fig-wt, @fig-pcv). Flagged groups
(@tbl-flags) are few and infection- rather than treatment-related.
Inference finds no plant or parasite signals (@tbl-other: weight p = 0.31 /
0.15; PCV p = 0.74 / 0.95) — efficacy here is parasitological, not confounded
by differential toxicity.


## 5.5. Objective v — comparative superiority

Exploration first: per-pair AUC differences (@fig-forest) scatter on both
sides of zero in both parasites — some pairs favour *A. indica*, others
*M. oleifera*, with no pattern by part or parasite. Inference confirms the
visual: paired W = 14, exact p = 1.0, HL ≈ 0.3 with 95% CI (−14.7, +20.5),
rank-biserial −0.14 (@tbl-sup); the motility cross-check agrees (p = 0.15).
With eight pairs the interval spans meaningful effects in both directions,
so the data cannot support a superiority claim — the honest conclusion is
the null, stated with its interval.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-sup
#| tbl-cap: Plant superiority contrasts (paired Wilcoxon; 8 pairs each).
fmt_contrast("plant_superiority.csv")
fmt_contrast("plant_superiority_motility.csv")
```

![Paired AUC difference per block with overall HL estimate](`r file.path(fig_dir, "plant_forest.png")`){#fig-forest}

![Paired block-mean AUC scatter](`r file.path(fig_dir, "plant_paired_auc.png")`){#fig-paired}

## 6. Diagnostics, sensitivity and refits

Three diagnostics were run. First, rank-test validity: several contrasts
contain tied absolute differences (all five *congolense* dose contrasts;
most motility contrasts) or dropped zero differences (superiority: one of
eight pairs). Because the exact Wilcoxon distribution is invalid with tied
ranks, every contrast records `n_nonzero`, `n_ties` and `p_method`, using
exact p-values only when clean and the continuity-corrected normal
approximation otherwise — this refit left all conclusions unchanged.
Second, paired-difference symmetry (@fig-sym): *evansi* differences sit
entirely below zero (a location shift, unproblematic); superiority
differences spread symmetrically around zero, matching its null. Third,
leave-one-block-out sensitivity (@tbl-loo): no single block flips any
conclusion (evansi top doses LOO p = 0.016 throughout; superiority LOO p
0.53–1.0). Completeness is enforced structurally at build (row counts and
part levels asserted).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-loo
#| tbl-cap: Leave-one-block-out sensitivity (stable = no single block flips the conclusion).
k("sensitivity_loo.csv")
```

![Paired differences: symmetry check (red = median)](`r file.path(fig_dir, "diagnostic_paired_diffs.png")`){#fig-sym}

## 7. Limitations

Group means of n = 3 mice erase within-group variance, so inference rests on
N = 16 blocks — power is low, intervals wide, description carries the
weight. Control identities/doses are unknown; Positive Control is a validity
reference only. Death-censored AUC flatters early-death groups, hence AUC is
always read with mortality. NA = death is conventional, worth confirming
against animal records. All results are exploratory, not confirmatory.
